newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY WHEAT, MAIZE FUTURES UP, BLACKSEED DOWN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY WHEAT, MAIZE FUTURES UP, BLACKSEED DOWN.

text.p: Maize and milling wheat futures prices rose on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Thursday but turnover remained below average, traders said.
The increase of maize futures prices was difficult to explain, one trader said.
"Compared with international prices and considering Hungary's bleak export possibilities current prices are already high enough," said Robert Vajo of Termin brokerage.
"But nobody wants to sell at lower prices and buyers seem to accept current levels for the moment," he added.
Vajo expected maize prices to start a slow downward movement in the coming weeks.

Old (1996) crop maize futures prices closed at between 19,000 forints to 19,300 forints for May and March, respectively, while new crop prices finished between 19,650 forints for October to 20,650 for December.

Milling wheat prices rose strongly for most maturities on the back of continued speculation about the damages ice cover could have done to the crop, despite most dealers' opinion that reliable predictions cannot be expected before mid-March.
"The rumours persist and continue to influence the market," Vajo said.
Widespread market talk about export possibilities to Serbia and Bosnia is also difficult to confirm, he added.

"Only small amounts could have gone there," he said, adding that present (BCE) price levels of around 29,000 forints for the 1996 crop are realistic while new crop prices will only have a factual base by the end of March.
"Until then, prices could go either way," Vajo said.
Blackseed prices continued their downward movement as traders expected the processors to announce purchase prices below the current market price of between 42,000 to 43,000 forints, he said.
Thursday's total turnover was 251 million forints or 505 contracts, of which 220 contracts were for maize and 200 for milling wheat.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
